definition: The XLNet was an autoregressive Transformer designed as an improvement over BERT, with 340M parameters and trained on 33 billion words.
details: It was released on 19 June 2019, under the Apache 2.0 license. It achieved state-of-the-art results on a variety of natural language processing tasks, including language modeling, question answering, and natural language inference.

explainer.lead: XLNet is an autoregressive Transformer designed as an improvement over BERT, with 340 million parameters and trained on 33 billion words. It matters because it reached state of the art on several NLP tasks when released.

tiers.eli5: It is a language model that learns by predicting words in many different orders instead of always left to right, so it sees text from more angles.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for tasks like question answering and natural language inference. The pitfall is that autoregressive pretraining is more complex to set up than BERT-style masked training.
tiers.paperLevel: An autoregressive Transformer with 340M parameters trained on 33 billion words, released 19 June 2019 under the Apache 2.0 license. It reported state-of-the-art results on language modeling, question answering and natural language inference.

explainer.example: On a natural language inference benchmark, XLNet surpassed the BERT-era baselines it was designed to improve on.
